summary: A shadow merge-queue signer for the signing host: two systemd user timers record every merge-queue entry (group tree, git merge-tree equality, a depth-1 predicted tree, the queue's own gate times and results) and sign host notes for the predicted or queued trees of our own authors with every local check, so tree equality, note-before-gate timing, run and slot-wait times and result agreement are measured. Host notes never cover merge_group runs, so that part skips and blocks nothing. A third timer, seed, runs st-test --seed on each new tip of main, signing and pushing the per-crate rust-tests notes of main's tree for the crates whose key has none, so pull requests reuse them.

replay.detail: No record or signature format changes: the notes are the ones st-test already makes.

schema.detail: No stored or wire format changes; the signer keeps its own local state files under ~/.local/state/evidence-queue-signer.

rules.detail: What counts as evidence is unchanged: the policy is not edited, and host notes still never cover a merge_group run. Seed makes the same per-crate notes st-test --seed makes by hand.

compatibility.detail: Nothing runs until the units are installed on a host.

manual.detail: On the signing host, after sign-off: copy scripts/evidence-queue-timer to ~/.local/bin and the six evidence-queue unit files to ~/.config/systemd/user, optionally write ~/.config/evidence-queue-signer/next-command, then systemctl --user enable --now evidence-queue-observe.timer evidence-queue-sign.timer evidence-queue-seed.timer (each on its own: seed does not need sign). The installed ~/.local/bin/evidence-queue-timer is the one file not read from main: a change to it needs a reinstall.

recovery.detail: touch ~/.config/evidence-queue-signer/off stops all three; systemctl --user disable --now the timers removes it.
